Definition: middle voice from G3954; to be frank in utterance, or confident in spirit and demeanor:--be (wax) bold, (preach, speak) boldly.
BiblicalUsage: Parrhesiazomai means to speak boldly, to be frank and confident in speech. Paul speaks boldly in the name of the Lord Jesus in Acts 9:28, and at Iconium Paul and Barnabas abide a long time speaking boldly in the Lord in Acts 14:3. Apollos begins to speak boldly in the synagogue at Ephesus in Acts 18:26, and Paul speaks boldly for three months in the synagogue there in Acts 19:8. The Greek text spells this word with a single rho after the prefix; the site's spelling doubles the rho, but it is the same verb.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe bold speech is the normal sound of the early church, from Paul to Apollos, and it was prayed for as much as it was practiced. My position is that if I cannot speak boldly for Christ, the problem is not my courage, it is my confidence in Him.
